evals.prompt: Define the domain terms for this billing service in a glossary the agents can read. Propose the table first.
evals.expected_output: Reads any existing docs/ai/specs/ubiquitous-language.md, the constitution, roadmaps, and PRDs, scans module, class, table, and route names, proposes a Term | Meaning here | Identifiers table, asks with request_user_input or one free-text question in an active chat, and writes the file only after confirmation.
expectations: Reads the existing terms document first when present and keeps its rows
Proposes rows with term, one-sentence meaning here, and the identifiers that carry it
asks with request_user_input or one free-text question in an active chat for a genuinely ambiguous term only, one at a time, recommendation first
Writes docs/ai/specs/ubiquitous-language.md only after the user confirms

evals.prompt: The spec says 'account' but the code says 'tenant' in half the modules. Pin the term and reconcile the names.
evals.expected_output: Proposes one term with the other spelling listed under Identifiers so the lint maps both, asks the user which term wins, and updates the document without deleting existing rows silently.
expectations: Lists both spellings under Identifiers of one term
Asks the user which term wins rather than deciding alone
Never deletes a row without naming the identifiers that lose their mapping

evals.prompt: Run the ubiquitous-language lint on my branch against origin/main and tell me what does not map.
evals.expected_output: Runs resolved_python <plugin-root>/scripts/ubiquitous-language-lint.py with --base origin/main, reports the JSON summary and each unmapped identifier with a suggested term or rename, and states that the lint is advisory and exits 0.
expectations: Reports each unmapped identifier with file, line, and a suggestion
States that the lint never blocks a gate
